In Charge of Regional/Sub-Regional
offices
Subject:
Avoding
CPFC from
being
made
a
respondent
in routine
manner in appeals and contempt cases pertaining to 7A/14B,
14 etc.- Regarding.
Sir,
It
has been experienced
that
Central
P.F. Commissioner
is invariably
impleaded as respondent in cases at different legal fora.
1. You are
requested
to
take
necessary
action
for
avoiding
Central
P.F.
Commissioner
from
being
made a respondent
in a routine
manner
in
appeals/contempt
cases pertaining to 7A/14B, 14 etc.
2. Often, there
is little
merit
in making CPFC a party
in either
of the two
categories of cases. Such inclusion of CPFC results in huge waste of time
and resources of the Organisation.
Beside, the matter sometimes escalates
to such a point that Courts pass Contempt Notice against CPFC. This can
be avoided to a certain extent by taking appropriate
legal steps.
3. With regard to the first category of case, the CPFCis neither an Appellate
Authority
nor is responsible for 7A /14B/Recovery
Orders passed by the
competent
Officers of the Regions. These are judicial
orders and can only
be appealed against in the higher court such as the EPFAppellate Tribunal
or a High Court. Hence, the inclusion of CPFCas one of Respondents is a
Misjoinder of party under Order 1 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
4. Similarly,
if the CPFCis made one of the Respondents on behalf of the CBT
( EPF) in the second category
of cases, then it can be pleaded by the
concerned
RO/SRO that the APFC/EO ( legal) of the concerned RO/SRO
signing the Written
Statement
on behalf of the Organisation
or the CBT
(EPF), is a competent authority to do so under Section-SE of the EPF& MP
Act and therefore there is no need to make CPFCOR ANY OTHEROfficer as
a Respondent in the case.

5. All the
ROs/SROs of EPFO requested to file
necessary applications
in
concerned Court for deletion of CPFC as a party,
in the first
instance
alongwith their Written Statement, the instructions must be followed in its
letterand
sprit.
Yours faithfully,
(J.R. Sharma)
Additional Central P.F. Commissioner (Legal)
